items.review_rationale: Reviewed the least finite projective resolution length, with infinity allowed if no finite such resolution exists. Distinguished a projective module from a projective resolution and checked the exactness conditions at each stage.

references.context: Homological algebra: exact augmented chain complex of projective R-modules resolving M

references.disposition: The projective dimension is minimized over finite resolutions and defined to be infinite if none exists, not the length of an arbitrary resolution.

items.review_rationale: Examined Ext_R^i(M,N) as ith cohomology of the Hom cochain complex induced by a free resolution of M. Hom here is R-linear and contravariant in the resolved module, with cohomology indexed by i.

references.context: Homological algebra: applying contravariant Hom to chain complex produces cochain complex

references.phrase: ith cohomology of a cochain complex
references.context: Homological algebra: kernel modulo image for an ith differential in a cochain complex

references.disposition: The superscript indexes cohomology, not ordinary ring exponentiation, and no particular free resolution is preferred.

items.review_rationale: Read the augmented unbounded chain complex with exactness at all displayed degrees and free modules at every F_i, not a finite projective resolution or the definition of Ext itself.

references.context: Module theory: free module over a ring with a basis and universal property
Homological algebra: chain complex with augmentation to target module and differential composites zero

references.disposition: Free implies projective under standard unital module conventions, but the definition explicitly chooses free rather than arbitrary projectives.

items.review_rationale: Read the representability/universal derivation property with d:S→Ω and the bijection Hom_S(Ω,M)≅Der_R(S,M) for every S-module. This is about module-valued derivations, not classical analytic differentials.

references.phrase: module of universal Kähler differentials Ω_{S/R}
references.context: Commutative algebra: universal S-module representing R-derivations

references.disposition: A natural universal Hom-versus-derivations bijection is required; checking a single target module is insufficient.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed additive, vanishing-on-base, and Leibniz axioms of a derivation D:S→M, relative to R→S. Unlike an arbitrary ring homomorphism, a derivation satisfies the product rule.

references.phrase: D vanishes on image of R
references.disposition: The derivation is R-relative; this restriction is stronger than additivity alone.
This Leibniz identity is the defining multiplicative compatibility, not multiplicativity of D.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the external-product test for Bourbaki properness: id_Z×f must be closed for every auxiliary topological space Z. This differs in setup from the relative-base-change definition of universally closed maps.

references.context: Topology: closed continuous map sending closed subsets of domain to closed subsets of codomain

references.disposition: The quantifier runs over all Z, not just discrete, compact, or base-change-over-Y spaces.

items.review_rationale: Read this Stacks-convention definition of proper topological map as requiring both separatedness of its diagonal and universal closedness. No equivalence to only compact inverse images is inferred.

references.disposition: Both conjuncts are required; separatedness is about the diagonal in X×_Y X, not ordinary Hausdorffness of X.

items.review_rationale: Read this quasi-proper convention as inverse images of quasi-compact subsets remaining quasi-compact; does not assert universal closedness or separatedness under other conventions.

references.context: Set theory/topology: preimage of a subset under a continuous map

references.disposition: The subset can be non-open, and the requirement is not the same as inverse images of closed sets being closed.
